parsed.why: No trans-specific criminalisation or border/facility exposure; Pride proceeds with police protection and courts grant trans document relief. Offsets: hostile senior-official rhetoric, one municipality fining Pride organisers, limited enforcement of protections.

Gender identity named in discrimination and hate-crime law, but enforcement uneven and hostility documented: 222 hate-speech incidents, attacks on a gender-nonconforming person, Pride needing 2,000 police. No traveler-facing criminal exposure.

Self-ID, protected facility access, hate-crime coverage, marriage equality and pride culture all currently in force; no traveler-facing restriction. Pending first-reading roll-back bills are political trajectory, not yet operative exposure.

Recent propaganda law criminalising LGBT visibility in public/media, zero anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime reporting since 2018, and documented impunity for bias violence against activists. Recourse thin; state chilling of visibility.

No criminalisation and courts recently rule for LGBT people (partnership, expression, foreign-spouse residence), but police failed assembly protection, hate-crime victim support is systemically lacking, and large hostile street mobilisation with Pride arrests.
